patch.objective: Using traffic-splitting strategies on Cloud Run or GKE: gradual rollouts, rollbacks, A/B testing

sources.cite: Google Cloud, Professional Cloud Developer certification exam guide: Section 1 Designing highly scalable, secure, and reliable cloud-native applications (~32%), Section 2 Building and testing (~23%), Section 3 Configuring for deployment (~24%), Section 4 Integrating with Google Cloud services (~21%)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the PDF on 2026-11-17 (no version or date printed). Quoted: 1.1 'Using traffic splitting strategies (e.g., gradual rollouts, rollbacks, A/B testing) on a new service on Cloud Run or GKE'; 1.3 'Creating signed URLs to grant access to Cloud Storage objects'.

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud Run: Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration (last updated 2026-11-10)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. Relevant text: roll back with 'gcloud run services update-traffic SERVICE --to-revisions REVISION=100'; 'Rolling back traffic to a revision updates the routing configuration immediately'; deploy with 'gcloud run deploy --image IMAGE --no-traffic' then shift traffic in steps, for example 5 percent; '--no-traffic --tag TAG_NAME' lets you 'directly test the new revision at a specific URL, without serving traffic'; 'the percentages must add up to 100'; 'traffic routing adjustments are not instantaneous'.
